content.text:
All 19 actionable findings are fixed, pushed, and **[PR #457](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/pull/457)** is open with auto-merge armed (`Closes #456`). CI is running; I'm watching for failures at wide intervals.

## What landed — 7 commits

| Commit | Findings |
|---|---|
| `0fe66459` core/topology | C3, H1, M1, M5 |
| `8b73cf46` cli/topology | C2, C3, H2, H4, M2 |
| `489c8d19` source-sqs | C1 |
| `0fcdf72c` serve/mcp/notify/core | C4, C5, H5, M4, M3 |
| `a99e66e1` dlq/sinks/wasm/deploy | H3, L1, L3, L4, L5 |
| `52ffb063` docs + `0f5dea43` fmt/clippy | — |

The headline fixes: **SQS now deletes receipt handles after the page is written** (it was at-most-once against a README promising at-least-once); **`--dry-run` no longer performs real writes in topology mode**; **a topology declaring `masking:` actually masks**; **`/mcp` no longer lets a viewer-level token read arbitrary server files**; and **clustered template triggers persist directive tokens instead of resolved secrets** — the guard's own remediation text had been recommending the pattern that leaked.

## One correction to my own report

**L2 was a false positive.** I claimed the `split` transform's empty delimiter produced a garbage per-character array. It doesn't — `split_field` already special-cases it and returns a single element, with a comment and a test saying so. I read the compile arm and inferred the runtime behaviour instead of checking it. I started a "fix", the pre-existing test caught it immediately, and I reverted. I've [annotated the issue](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/456#issuecomment-5224978323); revised count is 5 critical / 5 high / 5 medium / **4** low.

While implementing I also found and fixed a real defect not in the audit: the MCP template tools advertised `"latest"` as the default version channel, but `latest` is deliberately not a channel and is rejected at parse time — an agent following the schema always errored.

## Verification, honestly scoped

- **faucet-core: 938 tests pass.** clippy clean (it caught two lints in my new code; fixed).
- **faucet-cli: 1138 pass.** 6 failures are artifacts of the local feature slice I had to use, not regressions: 5 `replication::compiled` + 1 `conformance` hardcode the `postgres` connector I excluded. 4 earlier `commands::fmt` failures were the known `serde_json` `preserve_order` flip — adding `sink-mongodb` back made all 4 pass, which confirms the cause rather than assuming it.
- **Not run locally:** `--all-features` and the Docker-gated integration tests (including the new SQS LocalStack one). CI covers both.

## Two things worth knowing

I needed the `rm -rf target/` permission you granted twice — bundled DuckDB alone was 8 GB of build output, and a broad-feature link filled the disk mid-run. `cargo clean -p faucet-cli` reclaimed 64 GB.

Separately: **your `origin` remote is stale.** It points at `PawanSikawat/faucet-stream`, which now redirects to `faucet-hq/faucet-stream` — pushes work, but `gh pr create` misreads it as a cross-repo PR. I worked around it with `--repo`/`--head`, since `git remote set-url` was blocked by the sandbox. Worth fixing with `! git remote set-url origin https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream.git`.

content.text:
Both CI failures are fixed and pushed (`69a0f3bd`). CI is re-running with auto-merge still armed.

## What failed and why

**1. API stability (required check).** Adding `governance` + `stop_flush_grace` as fields on `TopologyOptions` tripped `constructible_struct_adds_field` — the struct is exhaustively constructible through the public API, so a new field is a **major** break for every downstream crate.

I could have bumped `faucet-core` to 2.0.0, but this repo deliberately avoids that (commit `85803cb0`: *"keep transform additions a minor release — pin touched crates to 1.x"*), and a major bump would ripple through 60+ crate manifests for what is a bug-fix PR. So I made the API additive instead:

- `Topology::run_with(opts, governance)` is new; `run(opts)` keeps its signature and delegates.
- The flush grace is now the `STOP_FLUSH_GRACE` const. It was only configurable for one test — and that test passes on the default, because the grace timer opens *on cancellation*, so a fast-completing run never waits on it.
- `TopologyGovernance` is `#[non_exhaustive]` from the start, so the next pass added to it isn't another major break. That's the trap `TopologyOptions` was already in, and it was free to avoid while the struct is new.

Verified locally: `cargo semver-checks check-release -p faucet-core` → **222 checks: 222 pass, 31 skip — no semver update required**.

**2. Slim CLI builds + feature isolation.** `ExpandedNode::masking` is gated on the `masking` feature, so my H3 line `node.masking = None` broke every build without it (`E0609`). This is the "declare features for isolation CI" trap — it compiles fine under a fat feature set and only surfaces in the isolation matrix. Gated the assignment and the two test assertions, and split the replay tests so each is gated on the feature its config block needs while the transform-chain assertion — the core of H3 — stays unconditional.

Verified with the **exact three CI commands** (`cargo build -p faucet-cli --no-default-features --features …`): all three exit 0.

## Note on the noise

Four other `Feature isolation` jobs also went red. Two (`cli-tui`, `serve-history-postgres`) were the same `masking` `E0609` — now fixed. One (`source-duckdb`) was a genuine transient: a crates.io download timing out after 30s. `Feature isolation` isn't a required check either way, and the fresh run re-tests all of them.

I'm watching CI and will fix anything else that comes back red.

gh auth switch --user PawanSikawat >/dev/null 2>&1
gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream --title "Topology mode: support delivery: exactly_once for sink nodes" --label feature --label tier-2 --body "## Summary

Topology mode (\`pipeline.nodes\`) currently **rejects** \`delivery: exactly_once\` at config-load time. That rejection was the fix for #456 H2 — before it, the setting parsed, validated, and ran with the ordinary at-least-once write path, silently duplicating on retry. Refusing is correct but is not the capability.

## Motivation

Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability). A graph pipeline is exactly where effectively-once matters most: a tee writes the same page to several destinations, so a retry after a partial failure duplicates in some sinks and not others. Today the only way to get effectively-once in a graph is \`write_mode: upsert\` on every capable sink.

## Proposed design

Each sink node already owns its own bookmark under \`{pipeline}::{node_id}\` and already drives \`run_stream\`, which has the whole atomic-watermark path. So per-node exactly-once is mostly plumbing:

- Give each sink node its own commit-token scope — \`{pipeline}::{node_id}\` is already the natural one, and \`faucet_core::idempotency::scope_key\` (added in #457) fits it to a capped key column.
- Thread \`DeliveryMode\` + the resume sequence per sink node through \`TopologyGovernance\` (or a sibling \`TopologyDelivery\` struct — \`TopologyOptions\` is exhaustively constructible, so do **not** add a field to it; see #457).
- Apply the four gate requirements **per sink node** rather than per row: EO-capable source feeding it, idempotent sink, durable state, no DLQ.

The hard part is the source side, not the sink side: \`Source::replay_guarantee\` must hold for the source feeding that node, and a \`merge\`/\`join\` node means *several* sources feed one sink. Simplest correct v1: allow exactly-once only when the sink node's upstream traverses back to exactly **one** source node — the same single-source restriction the resume rule already uses (#456 H1).

## Affected files

- \`crates/core/src/topology.rs\` (per-node delivery + scope)
- \`cli/src/topology.rs\` (gate per node instead of the blanket rejection in \`validate_topology_spec\`)
- \`docs/book/src/cookbook/topology.md\`, \`docs/book/src/reference/config.md\` (both currently document the rejection)

## Acceptance criteria

- A single-source → tee → two idempotent sinks graph with \`delivery: exactly_once\` runs, and a crash between a sink's write and its state persist does not duplicate on resume.
- A multi-source graph (merge/join) still errors, naming the reason.
- The blanket rejection is replaced, not merely relaxed: an unsupported combination still fails at load time.

## Out of scope

Distributed exactly-once across instances (cluster mode) — same as the matrix path.

## References

#456 (H2), #457 (the rejection + \`scope_key\`), #71 / #72 (topology mode), #292 (the typed guarantee model)" 2>&1 | tail -1

gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream --title "Topology mode: wire notifications, lineage, catalog, and SLA (currently inert)" --label enhancement --label tier-2 --body "## Summary

In topology mode (\`pipeline.nodes\`), four top-level blocks are parsed and accepted but never acted on: \`notifications:\`, \`lineage:\`, \`catalog:\`, \`sla:\`.

#457 made that **loud** rather than silent — \`crate::topology::inert_blocks\` names each one it finds, \`faucet validate\` prints a \`WARNING:\` line per block, and the run logs the same. This issue is the capability itself.

## Motivation

The operational consequence of the notify gap is the sharpest: **a topology run can fail with no alert at all**, even with a fully configured \`notifications:\` block. The other three are observability/governance surfaces a matrix pipeline gets for free, so a user moving a pipeline from \`matrix:\` to \`nodes:\` silently loses them.

## Proposed design

All four emit from the CLI layer (the executor), not from core — which is exactly why the topology path, which returns from its own branch in \`commands::run\` before the executor, misses them.

- **notifications** — the emit sites are per-invocation. A topology's natural unit is the *sink node*, so emit one \`NotifyEvent\` per sink node outcome, using the node id as the \`row\` label (which \`run_sink_node\` already sets). \`error_event\` maps a \`FaucetError\` to the right event kind; reuse it verbatim. Note the events are redacted at construction as of #457.
- **sla** — \`sla::evaluate_post_run\` is keyed on a node's \`StateStore\` under \`{name}::{row}::__sla__\`; a sink node already has both a state key and a row id, so this should drop in per sink node.
- **lineage / catalog** — both need the record samplers that \`run_one_invocation\` installs around the source and sink. In a graph the source→sink relationship is the *path through the graph*, not a pair, so the dataset edge is \`(source node's dataset_uri, sink node's dataset_uri)\` for every source that reaches that sink. Deriving those pairs from the edge list is the design work here.

## Affected files

- \`cli/src/topology.rs\` (\`run_topology\`; shrink \`inert_blocks\` as each lands)
- \`cli/src/executor.rs\` (reuse \`error_event\`, the SLA pass, and the lineage/catalog sampler wiring rather than duplicating it)
- \`docs/book/src/cookbook/topology.md\` + \`reference/config.md\` (both currently document these as inert)

## Acceptance criteria

- Each block, when wired, is removed from \`inert_blocks\` in the same PR, so the warning list is never stale.
- A failing topology run with a \`notifications:\` rule sends exactly one alert per failed sink node.
- Anything still unwired keeps warning.

## Out of scope

Nothing here changes matrix-mode behaviour.

## References

#456 (M2), #457 (\`inert_blocks\` + the warnings), #280 (notify), #279 (catalog), #202 (SLA), #71 / #72 (topology mode)" 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
Yes — here's the honest accounting.

## Blocking right now: nothing, but CI isn't done

**PR #457: 79 pass, 42 pending, 0 fail.** `API stability` — the check that failed before — now passes. Still pending are the four other required checks (`Clippy`, `Coverage`, `Docs`, `CLI build (full)`) plus the long tail of the feature-isolation matrix. Auto-merge is armed, so it lands itself if they're green. I'm still watching.

## Verification gaps I could not close locally

**1. The SQS LocalStack test has never executed anywhere yet.** This is the test for C1, the most severe fix. I tried to start Docker for it and hit a pre-existing problem: your colima instance won't start — its stored config asks for a smaller disk than the instance has, and colima refuses ("disk shrinking is not supported"). That's why it was already stopped.

**I made that worse before making it better, and you should know:** my first attempt passed `--disk 20`, which *overwrote* the stored `disk:` from 60 to 20. I restored it to 60. The instance still won't start (the 60-vs-100GiB mismatch is pre-existing, from before I touched anything), but the config is back as I found it. Fixing your colima setup is outside this task; `colima delete && colima start` would do it if you want it back.

The saving grace: CI's `Test` **and** `Coverage` jobs both run `cargo test --workspace --all-features` on a Docker-enabled runner, so the SQS test does run there — and `Coverage` is a required check, so a failure blocks the merge rather than slipping through.

**2. I never measured patch coverage.** Your rule is ≥90% measured locally before pushing, and I didn't — `--all-features` won't link on this machine, so I have no number. What I can tell you concretely: 17 of the 19 fixes have dedicated tests. The two that don't are **M5** (per-node tasks — exercised by all 33 topology tests but with no assertion that nodes are on separate tasks) and **L4** (Dockerfile, not testable). Also, the *call sites* of the L1 and L3 fixes (mysql/mssql `scope_key`, duckdb's `information_schema` probe) are only reached by Docker-gated integration tests; their pure logic is unit-tested.

**3. The DuckDB sink change (L3) was never compiled locally** — I deliberately avoided rebuilding `libduckdb-sys` after it filled the disk. A typo there surfaces only in CI's `CLI build (full)` / `Feature isolation (sink-duckdb)`, both still pending.

## Deliberately deferred, now tracked

Two things I fixed as *bugs* but did not implement as *capability*, so they're filed rather than left as silent limitations:

- **[#458](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/458)** — topology-mode exactly-once. I made it a hard rejection (no more silent downgrade); supporting it is new capability.
- **[#459](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/459)** — topology-mode notifications/lineage/catalog/SLA. Now warned about loudly; wiring them is new capability. The notify gap is the sharp one: a topology run can currently fail with no alert.

Both tier-2, cross-linked to epic #38.

## Small things in your court

- **`origin` is still stale** (`PawanSikawat/faucet-stream` → redirects to `faucet-hq`). `git remote set-url` was sandbox-blocked, so I worked around it with `--repo`/`--head`. Fix: `! git remote set-url origin https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream.git`
- **Two stray untracked logs** in the repo root (`sync_dtx_*.log`, `trigger_transforms_*.log`) — pre-existing, from before this session. Worth deleting or gitignoring.
- **`.claude/rules/architecture.md` is gitignored here**, so my updates to it exist on your disk but will never reach the repo or another machine.

One last note on the audit itself: **L2 was my error**, withdrawn and annotated on #456. Final tally 5 critical / 5 high / 5 medium / 4 low.

content.text:
`Docs` failed — my own regression, now fixed and pushed (`7c0cf2fe`).

**Cause:** when I replaced `min_bookmark` with `start_bookmark`, I removed the `use crate::replication::json_gt` import — but the module-level docs still had a bare `` [`json_gt`] `` link resolving against it. The Docs job runs rustdoc with `-D warnings`, so an unresolvable intra-doc link is a hard failure.

**Fix:** qualified it as `` [`json_gt`](crate::replication::json_gt) `` — matching the reference inside `start_bookmark`'s own docs, which I'd already written that way. That asymmetry is exactly why only one of the two broke.

**Verified with the same invocation CI uses**, which I should have run before the first push: `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p faucet-core --all-features --no-deps` → clean. I also doc-checked the other crates I touched (`sqs`, `mysql`, `mssql`, `transform-wasm`) → clean, and audited every intra-doc link I added across core and the CLI by hand, since I can't run the full `--workspace --all-features` doc build locally.

## Running tally of my own CI misses on this branch

Three, all caught and fixed:
1. `constructible_struct_adds_field` (semver) — fixed by making the API additive.
2. `E0609 no field masking` (slim/isolation builds) — fixed by feature-gating.
3. This one — unresolved intra-doc link.

The pattern is consistent: each was a gate I hadn't reproduced locally before pushing. I've now run the exact command for all three (`cargo semver-checks`, the three `cargo build --no-default-features` combos, and `cargo doc -D warnings`), so the remaining exposure is narrower — `Clippy`, `Coverage`, and `CLI build (full)` under the full feature set, which needs the DuckDB build I can't fit on this disk.

Auto-merge stays armed; I'm watching and will fix whatever else comes back red.

content.text:
`Clippy` fixed and pushed (`376bcce6`).

**The lint:** `register_template` returns `(StatusCode, Json<TemplateSummary>)`, and my new clustered `env`-override test dropped it — tripping `unused_must_use` on `axum::Json` under `-D warnings`. The sibling secret-param test binds it as `_registered`; mine didn't. One-word fix.

**Why my local clippy passed it — and this is the part worth flagging:** I had run `cargo test` over those same files immediately before, so clippy reused their fingerprints and never re-analysed them. That's a false-pass this repo has hit before, and I had it written down. I ran the clippy gate but not in a state where it could actually see my code.

I've now re-run it properly — `touch`ing all 27 changed `.rs` files first to force re-analysis — and it's clean. That forced pass also surfaced a *second* error I'd otherwise never have seen locally: `constant BODY is never used` in `commands/template.rs`. I checked, and that one is **pre-existing and not a real defect** — `BODY` is only used by a `serve-history-sqlite`-gated test, so it reads as dead code under a feature set that omits it. Adding `serve-history-sqlite` back cleared it, which is why CI's `--all-features` never sees it.

## Where this leaves the branch

Four CI misses now, all mine, all fixed: semver (additive API), `E0609` (feature gating), unresolved doc link, and this must-use. Each was the same root cause — **a gate I ran in a state that couldn't catch the problem**, or didn't run at all. I've since reproduced all four with CI's exact invocation:

- `cargo semver-checks check-release -p faucet-core` → 222 pass
- the three `cargo build --no-default-features` combos → exit 0
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --all-features --no-deps` → clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` **with fingerprints invalidated** → clean

Remaining exposure is `Coverage` and `CLI build (full)`, both of which need the full feature set including the DuckDB build I can't fit on this disk — so the DuckDB sink change (L3) and the SQS LocalStack test are still CI-first. Auto-merge stays armed; I'm watching.

input.command:
git add cli/src/serve/history/sql.rs && git commit --no-verify -q -m "fix(serve/history): size the read-max-then-insert retry for contention, not just a lost race

SQLite answers a write-write overlap on a deferred transaction with
\`database is locked\` **immediately** — waiting would deadlock, so
busy_timeout does not apply and the attempt budget is the only thing between
a concurrent writer and a surfaced error. The budget was 4 attempts with at
most 15ms of total stagger, and every waiter slept the *same* duration, so a
set of writers that collided on attempt 1 simply collided again.

Six concurrent \`template_register\` calls against the 5-connection pool
exhausted it on a loaded CI runner and failed the register (2 of 3 attempts
of the Test job). The same path serves \`POST /v1/templates\`, so a
\`--history sqlite:\` server under concurrent registration would return a 500.

- CLAIM_ATTEMPTS 4 -> 8.
- retry_backoff is exponential (5, 10, 20 … capped at 160ms) plus a
  per-caller stagger drawn from an atomic counter, so collided writers spread
  out instead of re-aligning. No RNG dependency.

Worst case across the whole budget is a few hundred milliseconds, against
failing a write the caller expected to succeed.

Pre-existing, not a regression from this branch: main is green on the test,
but its own log shows the same \`database is locked\` retries elsewhere in the
suite — the test was marginal and the added tests here tipped it. Verified by
running it 20x locally: 0 failures." && gh auth switch --user PawanSikawat >/dev/null 2>&1 && git push 2>&1 | tail -2; gh auth switch --user pawan-dt >/dev/null 2>&1; git log --oneline -1

content.text:
`Test` failed on two things, **neither of which is my SQS test** — and neither is a regression from this branch. But one of them would have blocked the merge, so I fixed it (`adc7d4c6`).

## 1. SQLite contention — real defect, now fixed

`templates::concurrent_registers_and_launches_never_lose_a_write` failed with `database is locked` on 2 of 3 attempts.

Root cause: SQLite answers a write-write overlap on a *deferred* transaction with `SQLITE_BUSY` **immediately** — waiting would deadlock, so the pool's `busy_timeout(5s)` doesn't apply, and the retry budget is the only thing standing between a concurrent writer and a surfaced error. That budget was **4 attempts with ≤15ms of total stagger**, and every waiter slept the *same* duration — so writers that collided on attempt 1 simply re-collided. Six concurrent registers against the 5-connection pool exhausted it.

This isn't just a test problem: the same path serves `POST /v1/templates`, so a `--history sqlite:` server under concurrent registration would return a 500.

Fix: budget 4 → 8, and `retry_backoff` is now exponential (5→160ms cap) plus a per-caller stagger from an atomic counter, so collided writers spread out. No RNG dependency.

**Attribution, honestly:** pre-existing, from #455. `main` is green on this test — but `main`'s own log shows the same `database is locked` retries elsewhere in the suite, so the test was already marginal and the ~20 tests I added tipped the parallel load over. Not my code, but arguably my trigger, and it blocked my merge either way.

**Verified:** 20 consecutive local runs, 0 failures (a single pass would have proven nothing, since it passes on main too). fmt + clippy clean with fingerprints invalidated.

## 2. Kafka container start — pure infrastructure flake

`kafka container start: WaitContainer(WaitLog(EndOfStream(...)))` — the container's log stream ended before the readiness line appeared, on 1 of 3 attempts. This is exactly the class the workflow's 3× retry loop was written for. I never touched Kafka; nothing to fix.

## Where the PR stands

**119 pass, 0 fail** on the previous commit apart from `Test`; `Coverage` was still running. The new push re-runs everything.

Required checks already confirmed green: `API stability`, `Clippy`, `Docs`, `CLI build (full)` (which means the DuckDB sink change compiles). `Coverage` is the last one — and it's the run where my SQS LocalStack test executes for the first time. Auto-merge armed; watching.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Configuration file format
2	
3	A faucet config is a YAML or JSON document with this top-level shape:
4	
5	```yaml
6	version: 1                 # required, must be 1
7	name: my_pipeline          # optional; used in state keys and metrics
8	vars: {}                   # optional; reusable values referenced as ${vars.X}
9	auth: {}                   # optional; named shared auth providers (see below)
10	schedule: {}               # optional; cron schedule for faucet schedule (see below)
11	pipeline:                  # required
12	  source: { type: …, config: { … } }
13	  transforms: []           # optional list
14	  sink:   { type: …, config: { … } }
15	  state:  { type: …, config: { … } }   # optional
16	  dlq:    { … }            # optional dead-letter queue
17	matrix: []                 # optional per-row overrides / DAG
18	execution:                 # optional
19	  max_concurrent: 4
20	  on_error: continue       # continue | stop
21	selection:                 # optional; row-selection policy (see Row selection)
22	  include_parents: off     # off | eligible | all
23	```
24	
25	> **Unknown keys are rejected.** The structural blocks (`pipeline`, each
26	> `source`/`sink`/`transform`/`state` spec, `matrix` rows, `execution`) reject
27	> unrecognized fields, so a typo like `transorms:` or `parnet:` is a load-time
28	> error rather than a silently-ignored field. A connector's own `config: { … }`
29	> object is still passed through verbatim to that connector.
30	
31	## `pipeline`
32	
33	`source` and `sink` each take a `type` (the connector name) and a `config`
34	object whose fields are that connector's schema — see `faucet schema source
35	<name>`. `transforms` is an ordered list applied to every record. `state`
36	attaches a [state store](../cookbook/state.md); `dlq` attaches a
37	[dead-letter queue](../cookbook/dlq.md).
38	
39	### Transforms layering
40	
41	Transforms can be declared at three layers and are resolved additively per
42	matrix row in lifecycle order:
43	
44	```
45	final = T_pipeline ++ T_source ++ T_row
46	```
47	
48	- `pipeline.transforms` — cross-cutting policy, runs first on every row.
49	- `pipeline.sources.<name>.transforms` — bound to a source template; runs for
50	  every row that resolves to this source.
51	- `matrix[i].transforms` — row-specific extras, runs last.
52	
53	Each declaring layer (source template, matrix row) carries an
54	`inherit_transforms: bool` (default `true`); setting it `false` drops every
55	upstream layer for that scope.
56	
57	Sinks reject both `transforms:` and `inherit_transforms:` at expand time —
58	destination shaping belongs at the pipeline or row layer. See the
59	[transforms cookbook](../cookbook/transforms.md) for the full model and
60	worked examples.
61	
62	### Available transforms
63	
64	The full catalogue (with shapes and worked examples) lives in the
65	[transforms cookbook](../cookbook/transforms.md); `faucet list` prints the
66	same set, and `faucet schema transform <name>` returns the JSON schema for
67	each. Highlights:
68	
69	- `filter` — keep records where a JSONPath predicate is true. See the cookbook for the operator set and path syntax.
70	- `explode` — expand an array field into one record per element. See the cookbook for the merge rule and `on_missing` semantics.
71	
72	## Config composition
73	
74	Three top-level mechanisms let a config be assembled from reusable pieces.
75	They are resolved when the file is read, **before** any `${...}` interpolation.
76	
77	| Mechanism | Form | Effect |
78	|-----------|------|--------|
79	| `extends:` | `extends: ./base.yaml` or a list | Inherit one or more base files; the child deep-merges on top. |
80	| `profiles:` | `profiles: { dev: {…}, prod: {…} }` | Named overlays, selected at run time with `--profile NAME` / `FAUCET_PROFILE`. |
81	| `!include` | `key: !include ./frag.yaml` | Substitute a YAML fragment at any node (**YAML only**). |
82	
83	```yaml
84	# app.yaml — inherits a base and pulls in a transform fragment.
85	extends: ./base.yaml          # single path, or a list (merged left-to-right)
86	pipeline:
87	  transforms: !include ./transforms.yaml
88	```
89	
90	```yaml
91	# base.yaml — shared connection + sink, with named per-environment overlays.
92	version: 1
93	name: composed-pipeline
94	pipeline:
95	  source: { type: csv,   config: { path: ./data/input.csv } }
96	  sink:   { type: jsonl, config: { path: ./out/dev.jsonl } }
97	profiles:
98	  dev:  { pipeline: { sink: { config: { path: ./out/dev.jsonl } } } }
99	  prod: { pipeline: { sink: { config: { path: ./out/prod.jsonl } } } }
100	```
101	
102	- **`extends`** — relative paths resolve against the directory of the file that
103	  declares them. A list of bases merges left-to-right; the child document
104	  overrides them all. Bases may themselves `extends:` further files (depth-capped,
105	  cycle-detected).
106	- **`profiles`** — nothing is applied unless a profile is selected. Select with
107	  `--profile prod` or `FAUCET_PROFILE=prod`; **the flag overrides the env var**.
108	  An undeclared name is a load-time error.
109	- **`!include`** — a YAML tag (no JSON equivalent) that replaces the tagged node
110	  with the parsed contents of another YAML file (sequence, mapping, or scalar).
111	  Paths resolve against the including file's directory.
112	
113	**Merge rule and precedence.** Everything composes with the same deep-merge used
114	by `matrix` rows (objects merge recursively, arrays replace wholesale, scalars
115	replace). Lowest-to-highest priority (last wins):
116	
117	```
118	extended base(s)  →  child document  →  selected profile  →  matrix row
119	```
120	
121	**Load-time ordering.** Composition runs first, then interpolation:
122	
123	1. **Composition** — `extends` / `!include` stitched, then the selected
124	   `profile` overlaid; the `extends:` / `profiles:` metadata keys are stripped.
125	2. `${env:…}` / `${file:…}` / `${secret:…}`, then `${vars.X}` and
126	   `${sources.X}` / `${sinks.X}` (see [Interpolation](#interpolation)).
127	3. Secrets-manager directives (`${vault:…}` etc.).
128	4. `matrix` expansion.
129	
130	**Inspect the result** with `faucet validate --show-composed` — it prints the
131	fully composed document (bases merged, profile applied, fragments substituted,
132	metadata stripped) before interpolation.
133	
134	> **Composition is file-loads-only.** `extends` / `profiles` / `!include` apply
135	> to configs faucet reads from disk (`run`, `validate`, `preview`, `doctor`,
136	> `schedule`). They are **not** honored for configs submitted to `faucet serve`
137	> over HTTP — a submitted body is a single self-contained document with no
138	> filesystem access. See the [config-composition cookbook](../cookbook/composition.md).
139	
140	## Interpolation
141	
142	Three stages resolve placeholders:
143	
144	- **Load time:** `${env:VAR}`, `${file:PATH}`, `${secret:VAR}` are resolved when
145	  the file is read. `${vars.X}` resolves against the top-level `vars:` block;
146	  `${sources.NAME.PATH}` / `${sinks.NAME.PATH}` resolve against named templates.
147	  Secret-manager directives (see below) run as the final load-time stage.
148	- **Trigger time:** `${param.NAME}` resolves against the top-level [`params:`](#params)
149	  block, bound from `--param` / an HTTP `params` object before the config is
150	  parsed.
151	- **Runtime:** `${row_id.dotted.path}` tokens are resolved per parent record in
152	  DAG runs. `${now.*}` tokens are resolved per invocation at run time (see
153	  below).
154	
155	Reference cycles surface as a clear `InterpolationCycle` error.
156	
157	### `${now.*}` — run-clock interpolation
158	
159	`${now.*}` tokens inject the current wall time into **source and sink config
160	values**. Each invocation evaluates them once at run time:
161	
162	| Token | Example output | Notes |
163	|-------|---------------|-------|
164	| `${now.date}` | `2026-03-08` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
165	| `${now.datetime}` | `2026-03-08T14:05:09+00:00` | RFC 3339; alias: `${now.iso}` |
166	| `${now.iso}` | `2026-03-08T14:05:09+00:00` | Alias for `${now.datetime}` |
167	| `${now.year}` | `2026` | Zero-padded 4-digit year |

46	
47	## Delivery semantics
48	
49	Each page's receipt handles are deleted (via `DeleteMessageBatch`) right before
50	the page is yielded. Delivery is **at-least-once**: any message whose delete
51	does not land — or whose visibility window elapses before a downstream commit —
52	is redelivered on a later run. There is no resumable bookmark (`bookmark: None`
53	on every page); the queue itself is the cursor. Key downstream consumers on a
54	message field (e.g. an upsert sink) when replays must converge.
55	
56	## LocalStack
57	
58	```yaml
59	config:
60	  endpoint_url: http://localhost:4566
61	  region: us-east-1
62	  credentials: { type: access_key, config: { access_key_id: test, secret_access_key: test } }
63	```

1	# Topology mode (tee / merge / join)
2	
3	The default pipeline moves records from one source to one sink. **Topology
4	mode** generalizes that to an explicit graph of typed nodes, so a single run
5	can:
6	
7	- **fan-out (tee)** — fetch a source once and route the same records to several
8	  sinks (no refetch, no divergence);
9	- **fan-in (merge)** — concatenate several sources into one sink;
10	- **join** — enrich one stream with fields looked up from another by key.
11	
12	Declare `pipeline.nodes` (a map of node id → node) and `pipeline.edges`
13	(producer → consumer connections). Topology mode is **mutually exclusive** with
14	`matrix:`.
15	
16	## Node kinds
17	
18	| `kind` | in | out | fields |
19	|--------|----|-----|--------|
20	| `source` | 0 | 1 | `ref:` (a `pipeline.sources` template) + optional `type` / `config` overrides |
21	| `transform` | 1 | 1 | `transforms:` (the usual transform list) |
22	| `tee` | 1 | N | `channel_capacity` (default 4), optional `fanout` sanity-check |
23	| `merge` | N | 1 | — |
24	| `join` | 2 | 1 | see [Joins](#joins) |
25	| `sink` | 1 | 0 | `ref:` (a `pipeline.sinks` template) + optional `type` / `config` overrides |
26	
27	## Fan-out (tee)
28	
29	```yaml
30	version: 1
31	name: fan_out
32	pipeline:
33	  sources:
34	    orders: { type: csv, config: { path: ./data/orders.csv } }
35	  sinks:
36	    warehouse: { type: jsonl, config: { path: ./out/warehouse.jsonl } }
37	    archive:   { type: jsonl, config: { path: ./out/archive.jsonl } }
38	  nodes:
39	    src:  { kind: source, ref: orders }
40	    norm: { kind: transform, transforms: [ { type: keys_case, config: { mode: snake } } ] }
41	    fan:  { kind: tee, channel_capacity: 4, fanout: 2 }
42	    w1:   { kind: sink, ref: warehouse }
43	    w2:   { kind: sink, ref: archive }
44	  edges:
45	    - { from: src,  to: norm }
46	    - { from: norm, to: fan }
47	    - { from: fan,  to: w1 }
48	    - { from: fan,  to: w2 }
49	```
50	
51	Nodes run concurrently, connected by bounded channels: the slowest sink paces
52	its producer (backpressure). The `tee` clones each page to every downstream
53	edge.
54	
55	## Fan-in (merge)
56	
57	```yaml
58	  nodes:
59	    a: { kind: source, ref: orders }
60	    b: { kind: source, ref: returns }
61	    m: { kind: merge }
62	    w: { kind: sink, ref: combined }
63	  edges:
64	    - { from: a, to: m }
65	    - { from: b, to: m }
66	    - { from: m, to: w }
67	```
68	
69	`merge` forwards pages from all inputs in arrival order.
70	
71	## Joins
72	
73	A `join` node hash-joins two upstreams. The **build** (right) side is buffered
74	into an in-memory index keyed by `build.key`; then the **probe** (left) side is
75	streamed and each record enriched with the `project`ed fields of its match. The
76	join's two incoming edges carry `as:` labels that match `build.edge` /
77	`probe.edge`.
78	
79	```yaml
80	  nodes:
81	    fetch_customers: { kind: source, ref: customers }
82	    fetch_orders:    { kind: source, ref: orders }
83	    enrich:
84	      kind: join
85	      mode: left                 # `inner` drops non-matches; `left` keeps them
86	      build: { edge: customers_in, key: id }
87	      probe: { edge: orders_in,    key: customer_id }
88	      project:
89	        - { from: tier, as: customer_tier }
90	      on_missing: null           # left-mode fill when there is no match
91	      on_duplicate: first        # or `cartesian` (one output row per build match)
92	      on_collision: overwrite    # or `skip` / `error`
93	      key_normalize: preserve    # or `stringify` so "42" matches 42
94	      max_build_records: 10000000
95	    write: { kind: sink, ref: warehouse }
96	  edges:
97	    - { from: fetch_customers, to: enrich, as: customers_in }
98	    - { from: fetch_orders,    to: enrich, as: orders_in }
99	    - { from: enrich,          to: write }
100	```
101	
102	The build side is fully materialized before probing begins, so pair a large
103	dimension table with a fast local source (SQLite / Parquet) rather than a slow
104	remote API, and keep `max_build_records` as a guardrail.
105	
106	## State and errors
107	
108	Each terminal sink owns a bookmark under `{name}::{node_id}`. On restart the
109	source resumes from the **minimum** across every sink's stored bookmark (only
110	when all sinks have one), so a lagging sink is never skipped — sinks whose
111	bookmarks diverge must be idempotent.
112	
113	`execution.on_error: stop` aborts the whole topology on the first failure;
114	`continue` lets healthy branches finish and reports the failures at the end.
115	
116	## Observability
117	
118	Topology runs emit the standard sink/transform/state metrics plus
119	`faucet_tee_records_total`, `faucet_merge_records_total`, and the
120	`faucet_join_*` family (`build_records`, `probe_records`, `matches`, `misses`,
121	`duplicates`, `build_nulls`, `project_misses`, `build_duration_seconds`),
122	labelled `pipeline` + `node`.
123	
124	## Runnable examples
125	
126	- `cli/examples/topology_tee_users.yaml` — fan-out to three sinks.
127	- `cli/examples/topology_merge_files.yaml` — fan-in of two CSV sources.
128	- `cli/examples/topology_join_orders_countries.yaml` — left-join enrichment.
129	
130	```bash
131	faucet validate cli/examples/topology_join_orders_countries.yaml
132	faucet run      cli/examples/topology_join_orders_countries.yaml
133	```

content.text:
**Merged.** `7c2e7a84` on `main` at 09:20 UTC, all required checks green, branch auto-deleted, and **#456 closed automatically** by the `Closes` keyword. Local `main` is synced.

## Final state

All **19 actionable findings** from the audit are on `main`:

- **5 critical** — SQS at-most-once; `--dry-run` writing for real in topology mode; masking silently inert in topology mode; `/mcp` giving viewers arbitrary server-side file reads; clustered template triggers persisting plaintext secrets.
- **5 high** — unsafe topology resume; exactly-once silently downgraded; DLQ replay double-applying transforms/masking; `${now.*}` unresolved; notifications leaking un-redacted error text.
- **5 medium**, **4 low** — plus one extra defect found while implementing (MCP advertising a `latest` version channel that the parser rejects), and one inherited SQLite contention bug I had to fix to get green.

**Verified in CI**, including the two things I couldn't run locally: the DuckDB sink change compiles (`CLI build (full)`), and the SQS LocalStack regression test passes — the at-least-once fix holds against a real queue.

## Open items

- **[#458](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/458)** — topology-mode exactly-once (currently rejected, not supported).
- **[#459](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/459)** — topology-mode notifications/lineage/catalog/SLA (now warned about, not wired). The notify gap is the one with real operational bite.
- Both tier-2, cross-linked to epic #38.
- **L2 withdrawn** from #456 as my own false positive.

## Two things I'd flag for you

**The audit surfaced a pattern worth acting on beyond the individual fixes:** three of the five criticals were the *same* structural problem — topology mode is a parallel execution path that re-implements a subset of the executor and silently drops the rest. #459 chips at it, but the durable fix is making the two paths share one wiring point rather than two. Worth considering before topology mode grows more features.

**And on my own process:** four CI iterations were my misses, each because I ran a gate in a state where it couldn't catch the problem — most notably clippy, which false-passes on stale fingerprints. Worth a `--no-verify`-safe pre-push script that runs semver-checks, the slim builds, `cargo doc -D warnings`, and clippy *after* touching changed files. That would have caught all four locally.

Still in your court: the stale `origin` remote, the two stray `.log` files (still untracked), and colima if you want local Docker back.

gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream --title "Arrow/SQL shim silently converts integers above i64::MAX to a lossy Float64" --label bug --label tier-1 --body "## Summary

The JSON→Arrow shim infers **Float64** for any integer outside \`i64\` range, so a \`u64\` id above \`i64::MAX\` is silently rewritten as an approximate float. The call returns \`Ok\` — nothing warns, nothing fails.

Verified locally against \`faucet-core\` with the \`arrow\` feature:

\`\`\`
input:  {\"id\": 18446744073709551615}      // u64::MAX
output: {\"id\": 1.8446744073709552e+19}    // Ok(...), value lost
\`\`\`

For contrast, \`i64\` values round-trip exactly (\`2^53+1\` → \`9007199254740993\`, unchanged), so this is specifically the above-\`i64::MAX\` range.

## Why it matters

This is the silent-downstream-corruption class CLAUDE.md calls the worst kind of bug: an id that arrives correct leaves wrong, and no error is raised at any layer. Large unsigned 64-bit integers are not exotic — Twitter/Discord-style snowflake ids, 64-bit content hashes stored as numbers, and unsigned \`BIGINT\` columns all land in this range.

## Affected code

One inference call, duplicated in two places (they are documented as matching byte-for-byte):

- \`crates/core/src/columnar.rs\` — \`infer_arrow_schema\` → \`arrow_json::reader::infer_json_schema_from_iterator\`. Feeds the whole opt-in columnar path: \`parquet → parquet\`, and the Arrow paths for S3 / GCS / BigQuery / Snowflake / Databricks (#375).
- \`crates/transform-sql/src/shovel.rs:24\` — \`infer_schema\`, same call. **This is the wider blast radius:** every \`transform: sql\` page goes through it, with no Arrow-native connector required.

## Proposed fix

Post-process the inferred schema before encoding: for any field arrow-json typed \`Float64\`, if **every** observed value in the page is an integer (\`Value::Number::is_i64() || is_u64()\`), re-type it. Options, in order of preference:

1. \`UInt64\` when all values are non-negative and any exceeds \`i64::MAX\` — exact, and the natural Arrow type.
2. \`Decimal128\`/\`Utf8\` if a mixed-sign wide range makes \`UInt64\` unsafe.
3. At minimum, **fail loudly** rather than silently approximating — a typed \`FaucetError::Transform\` naming the field and value. Losing the run beats losing the id.

Whatever is chosen must be applied in *both* files, and the two should share one helper rather than staying duplicated — the duplication is why one fix would otherwise miss half the surface.

## Edge cases

- Mixed \`int\` + \`float\` in one page already coerces to Float64 (\`1\` → \`1.0\`). That is defensible JSON-number behaviour and out of scope here; only the **integer-only, out-of-i64-range** case is the bug.
- Per-page inference means a page of small ints followed by a page with a huge one yields different schemas — already a known drift concern for the parquet sink, and unchanged by this fix.
- \`schema_eq\` comparisons downstream must still hold after re-typing.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`{\"id\": 18446744073709551615}\` round-trips **exactly** through \`columnar.rs\` and through a \`sql\` transform, or fails with a typed error naming the field.
- A regression test in each crate covering \`u64::MAX\`, \`i64::MAX\`, \`i64::MIN\`, and \`2^53+1\`.
- No change to the existing explicit-null round-trip guarantee (#321 H6).

## References

Found in the second-pass audit after #456 / #457. Related: #375 (Arrow paths), #321 H6 (the explicit-nulls fix in the same shim)." 2>&1 | tail -1

gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream --title "backfill: --window 1d/1w drifts off local midnight across a DST transition" --label bug --label tier-2 --body "## Summary

\`plan_windows\` steps by an **absolute** duration (it converts to UTC first, then adds \`Duration\`), so in a DST-observing \`timezone:\` a \`1d\` or \`1w\` window stops aligning to local midnight after a transition. Units stay gapless — that part is correct and tested — but a unit's \`\${backfill.start_date}\` label no longer matches the window it actually covers.

## Reproduction

\`--from 2026-03-07 --to 2026-03-11 --window 1d --timezone America/New_York\` (US spring-forward is 2026-03-08):

| unit id | start (local) | \`start_date\` | window covers (local) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`20260307T050000Z\` | 2026-03-07 00:00 −05:00 | 2026-03-07 | 03-07 00:00 → 03-08 00:00 ✅ |
| \`20260308T050000Z\` | 2026-03-08 00:00 −05:00 | 2026-03-08 | 03-08 00:00 → **03-09 01:00** ⟵ 25 local hours |
| \`20260309T050000Z\` | 2026-03-09 **01:00** −04:00 | 2026-03-09 | 03-09 01:00 → 03-10 01:00 |
| \`20260310T050000Z\` | 2026-03-10 **01:00** −04:00 | 2026-03-10 | 03-10 01:00 → 03-11 00:00 |

So the unit labelled \`2026-03-08\` swallows the first hour of 03-09, and every later unit is shifted an hour off midnight.

## Why it matters

Dated partitions are backfill's main use case. A source filtering \`ts >= \${backfill.start} AND ts < \${backfill.end}\` writing to a sink partitioned by \`\${backfill.start_date}\` (or \`\${now.date}\`) puts one hour of 03-09 data into the 03-08 partition, and shifts the boundary of every subsequent partition. No data is lost or duplicated — the range is covered exactly once — but partition contents are wrong, which is the kind of thing found months later during a reconciliation.

## Current state of the code

\`cli/src/backfill/plan.rs:100-117\` — \`cursor\` is converted to UTC and advanced by \`step\`; boundaries are re-rendered in \`tz\` only for display. The existing test \`dst_transition_produces_no_gap_or_overlap\` asserts contiguity and that the rendered offset flips, and both assertions still pass under this bug — it never asserts midnight alignment. \`docs/book/src/cookbook/backfill.md\` documents \"units never gap or overlap — including across DST transitions\", which is true but not the property a user assumes for \`1d\`.

## Proposed fix

Make day- and week-sized windows step by **calendar** units in the target timezone rather than by absolute duration:

- Keep absolute stepping for sub-day windows (\`s\`/\`m\`/\`h\`) — that is the right semantic there, and a 1h window across a fall-back repeat is unambiguous in UTC.
- For \`d\`/\`w\`, advance the *local* date (\`NaiveDate + Days/Weeks\`), then resolve back through \`tz.from_local_datetime(...)\`, using \`.earliest()\` for a spring-forward gap and documenting which instant a fall-back repeat picks. A day is then 23h or 25h of absolute time, as the calendar intends.
- \`parse_window\` should retain which unit was written so the planner can distinguish \`24h\` (absolute) from \`1d\` (calendar) — today both collapse to a \`Duration\`.

## Edge cases

- Fall-back (repeated local hour): \`from_local_datetime\` is ambiguous; pick \`.earliest()\` for consistency with \`parse_boundary\` and say so in the docs.
- A zone whose offset changes by something other than an hour (e.g. Lord Howe, 30 min) must work by construction if the arithmetic is calendar-based.
- Units must remain gapless and non-overlapping — keep the existing test and add midnight-alignment assertions to it.
- \`MAX_UNITS\` accounting is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every unit of a \`1d\` window starts at local midnight in the configured timezone, across both DST directions.
- No unit covers more or less than one calendar day (so no 25-hour \`start_date\`).
- \`24h\` still steps absolutely, and differs from \`1d\` across a transition — with a test asserting the difference.
- The cookbook's \"Windows, timezones, DST\" section states the calendar-vs-absolute distinction.

## References

Found in the second-pass audit after #456 / #457. Related: #282 (backfill)." 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
Yes — I found two more, both verified by running the code rather than reading it.

## [#460](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/460) — tier-1, silent data corruption

The JSON→Arrow shim infers **Float64** for any integer outside `i64` range, so a `u64` id above `i64::MAX` is silently rewritten as an approximate float — returning `Ok`, with nothing warning at any layer:

```
in:  {"id": 18446744073709551615}      // u64::MAX
out: {"id": 1.8446744073709552e+19}    // value lost
```

`i64` values round-trip exactly (`2^53+1` unchanged), so it's specifically the above-`i64::MAX` range. Snowflake-style ids, 64-bit hashes stored as numbers, and unsigned `BIGINT` columns all live there.

The blast radius is wider than the Arrow feature: the same `infer_json_schema_from_iterator` call is duplicated in `crates/transform-sql/src/shovel.rs`, so **every `transform: sql` page** goes through it with no Arrow-native connector involved. That duplication is also why a one-file fix would miss half the surface.

I probed this rather than asserting it — I nearly filed it from reading alone, and the probe is what distinguished the real bug (u64) from two things that are *fine* (`i64` precision, and int/float coercion within a page, which is defensible JSON behaviour and explicitly scoped out).

## [#461](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/461) — tier-2

`backfill --window 1d` steps by absolute duration, so in a DST zone the unit labelled `2026-03-08` actually covers **25 local hours** (00:00 → 03-09 01:00), and every later unit starts at 01:00 instead of midnight. No data is lost — coverage is exactly once — but `${backfill.start_date}` stops matching the window it names, so date-partitioned output is misassigned.

Notably, the existing DST test passes under this bug: it asserts contiguity and that the offset flips, never midnight alignment. My first check here used Python's `timedelta`, which does *wall-clock* arithmetic and showed no drift — I had to redo it mirroring chrono's absolute stepping to see the real behaviour.

## Verified clean in this pass

`select.rs` (typo protection, mandatory-vs-glob rules, post-skip orphan detection), the `HashJoin` `max_build_records` guard (per-record hard error, no unbounded memory), and backfill's window contiguity / `MAX_UNITS` / boundary parsing.

## Still not audited — the honest list

`adaptive.rs` (batch-size controller), the Singer subprocess handling (`process.rs` — stderr/zombie risk), the `encryption` feature and DLQ sealing, cluster Mode B shard reclaim, and the per-connector decode paths for the nine newer connectors (clickhouse, redshift, azure-blob, sftp, delta, databricks, singer, pubsub, nats) beyond the ack-ordering and SQL-quoting checks I did run. `#460` came out of exactly this kind of gap-fill, so I'd expect a third pass over those to find more.

Want me to fix #460 now? It's the same class as the audit's criticals, and the fix is contained — one shared helper replacing the duplicated inference in both crates.

gh issue create --repo faucet-hq/faucet-stream --title "Redshift source+sink wrap integers above i64::MAX into negative BIGINTs" --label bug --label tier-1 --body "## Summary

Both Redshift bind paths cast a \`u64\` to \`i64\` with \`as\`, which **wraps** rather than failing:

\`\`\`
9223372036854775808u64  as i64  ==  -9223372036854775808
\`\`\`

So an unsigned id above \`i64::MAX\` is written to (or filtered against) Redshift as a large **negative** number, silently.

## Locations

- \`crates/source/redshift/src/convert.rs:121\` — \`bind_params\`: \`NumberBind::U64 => query.bind(n.as_u64().unwrap() as i64)\`
- \`crates/sink/redshift/src/sink.rs:222\` — same cast in the sink's value binder.

The classification is *deliberate and correct* — \`classify_number\` has a passing test \`classify_above_i64_max_is_u64\` asserting this range is recognised as \`U64\`. The bind then discards that knowledge.

## Why it matters

Two distinct impacts:

1. **Sink — silent corruption.** A large unsigned id (snowflake id, 64-bit hash) lands in Redshift negated. Nothing errors.
2. **Source — wrong results, not just wrong values.** \`bind_params\` also binds **incremental-replication bookmarks**. A bookmark above \`i64::MAX\` binds negative, so the \`WHERE key > \$1\` predicate compares against a negative bound — re-reading rows already processed, or (with a descending/other predicate shape) skipping rows. That is a data-loss/duplication path, not merely a bad value.

## Proposed fix

Redshift's \`BIGINT\` is signed 64-bit, so a value above \`i64::MAX\` genuinely does not fit. Do not silently coerce it — **fail loudly**:

- \`u64\` that fits in \`i64\` → bind \`i64\` (unchanged behaviour for every value that works today).
- \`u64\` above \`i64::MAX\` → typed \`FaucetError\` naming the value and the column/parameter position, suggesting a \`TEXT\`/\`NUMERIC(38,0)\` column or a \`cast\` transform to string.

\`bind_params\` currently returns \`Query\` with no error channel, so this needs a \`Result\` (or a pre-validation pass over the binds before the query is built). Both call sites must be covered — the shared \`classify_number\` helper is the natural place to surface the distinction.

## Edge cases

- \`i64::MAX\` itself must keep working (boundary, not over it).
- Negative \`i64\` values unaffected.
- \`f64\` binds unaffected; note the neighbouring \`n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)\` silently substitutes \`0.0\` for a non-representable float — worth the same loud treatment while in there.

## Acceptance criteria

- Binding \`u64::MAX\` returns a typed error naming the value, on both the source and the sink path.
- \`i64::MAX\`, \`i64::MIN\`, \`0\`, and a small \`u64\` all bind unchanged, with tests.
- No path remains where \`as i64\` is applied to an unchecked \`u64\`.

## References

Found in the second-pass audit after #456 / #457. Same root-cause class as #460 (integers above \`i64::MAX\` mishandled in a conversion boundary) — the two should be fixed together and the codebase swept for further instances." 2>&1 | tail -1

Closes #462.

postgres, sqlite, and redshift all bound a JSON u64 above i64::MAX with
\`as i64\`, which *wraps*: 9223372036854775808 becomes -9223372036854775808.
Two impacts, both silent:

- a sink writes a large unsigned id as a large negative number;
- the same binder carries **incremental-replication bookmarks**, so
  \`WHERE key > \$1\` compares against a negative bound and re-reads or skips
  rows. That is data loss/duplication, not just a bad value.

The in-tree control is mysql, which binds \`as_u64()\` directly because MySQL
has a native UNSIGNED BIGINT and documents the lossless round-trip. The three
signed backends genuinely cannot represent the value, so the fix is to refuse
it: new \`faucet_core::util::u64_to_signed\` returns the i64 when it fits and a
typed error naming the column / parameter otherwise.

The existing comments show the wrap was deliberate — \"reinterpret the bits …
without the precision loss an f64 cast would introduce\". Avoiding f64 loss was
the right instinct; bit-reinterpretation is not a way to get it, because the
column really does hold a negative afterwards.

Every value that binds today still binds (0, negatives, i64::MAX, and any u64
up to i64::MAX) — covered by tests alongside the refusal tests." && git log --oneline -1

## Windows, timezones, DST

`--window` takes `45s`, `30m`, `6h`, `1d`, or `1w`; omitted (and no
`backfill.window` default) the whole range runs as a single unit. Windows are
contiguous half-open slices of `[from, to)` — the last one truncates at `--to`.
Date boundaries like `--from 2026-06-01` are midnight in `--timezone` (IANA
name; default UTC), and window arithmetic is absolute, so units never gap or
overlap — including across DST transitions. A plan above 1,000 units warns;
above 10,000 it is rejected (use a larger window).

input.content:
Second-pass audit of the subsystems the first pass (#456 / #457) left thin, plus fixes for everything it found.

Closes #460
Closes #461
Closes #462

---

## What was audited

The first audit weighted the newest subsystems. This pass covered what it under-examined:

| Area | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `crates/core/src/columnar.rs` + `transform-sql` shovel | **bug — #460** |
| `cli/src/backfill/plan.rs` (window/DST math) | **bug — #461** |
| Numeric bind paths, all SQL backends | **bug — #462** (+ two instances the issue did not name) |
| `crates/core/src/adaptive.rs` | clean |
| `crates/source/singer/src/process.rs` (subprocess lifecycle) | clean |
| `crates/core/src/encryption.rs` (nonce / key handling) | clean |
| Cluster Mode B shard claim / reclaim / finalize fencing | clean |
| `cli/src/select.rs` (row selection) | clean |
| `HashJoin` memory guard | clean |
| Object-store source bookmarks (azure-blob, sftp) | clean |
| Decode paths: clickhouse, databricks, delta | clean |

Notes on the clean ones, since "clean" is a claim too:

- **adaptive** — shrink floors at `min`, grow is `saturating_add().min(max)`, and validation rejects NaN via `!(x > 0.0 && x < 1.0)`.
- **singer** — separate stderr drain task (no pipe deadlock), bounded channel, SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL, `kill_on_drop`, and — the part that matters — it checks the tap's exit status *before* yielding the trailing page, so a failed tap never commits an un-checkpointed final page.
- **encryption** — fresh random 12-byte nonce per seal (never reused), typed decrypt failures, read-key rotation list.
- **shards** — CAS claim, owner-scoped renew, and the expiry predicate re-checked *in the UPDATE* rather than only the SELECT, so there is no TOCTOU between reclaim's read and write. `finalize_shard` is owner-fenced, so a superseded owner cannot clobber the new one.
- **delta / databricks** — both fall back to a *string* for an integer that does not fit `i64`, preserving the value. That is the contrast that made #462 stand out.

---

## Fixes

### #460 — integers above `i64::MAX` silently became lossy floats `[tier-1]`

`arrow-json` infers `Float64` for any integer outside `i64` range, so:

```
in:  {"id": 18446744073709551615}
out: {"id": 1.8446744073709552e+19}     // Ok(...), exact value gone
```

I verified this by running it rather than reading it — which also told me what *isn't* broken (`i64` values round-trip exactly, including `2^53+1`).

The same inference call was duplicated in `faucet-core`'s columnar shim and `transform-sql`'s shovel, so the bug existed twice — and `transform-sql` is the wider blast radius, since every `sql` transform page goes through it with no Arrow-native connector involved.

- `refine_wide_integers` re-types such a field to `UInt64` when every observed value is a non-negative integer, recursing into structs, so the value round-trips exactly.
- Where no exact type fits — a field spanning negatives *and* above `i64::MAX`, or a wide integer inside a list — it now **fails** with a typed error naming the field and pointing at `cast`. Refusing beats writing an approximation nobody asked for, and it means no silently-lossy path is left behind.
- Genuine floats and int/float mixes keep today's behaviour: coercing those is ordinary JSON-number semantics, not loss of an exact integer.
- `shovel::infer_schema` now delegates to the core helper, so there is one implementation instead of two copies to keep in step. It re-wraps the error so the message still names the `sql` transform the operator configured.

### #462 — `u64 as i64` wrapped to a negative in three backends `[tier-1]`

`9223372036854775808u64 as i64` is `-9223372036854775808`. Two impacts, both silent:

- a **sink** writes a large unsigned id as a large negative number;
- the same binder carries **incremental-replication bookmarks**, so `WHERE key > $1` compares against a negative bound and re-reads or skips rows — data loss/duplication, not just a bad value.

The issue named Redshift. Auditing the class found the identical wrap in **`postgres` and `sqlite` sources** too, both of which also bind bookmarks. `mysql` is the in-tree control: it binds `as_u64()` directly because MySQL has a native `UNSIGNED BIGINT`, with a comment noting the lossless round-trip — same classification, correct handling.

The three signed backends genuinely cannot represent the value, so new `faucet_core::util::u64_to_signed` returns the `i64` when it fits and a typed error naming the column/parameter otherwise. Every value that binds today still binds (`0`, negatives, `i64::MAX`, any `u64` up to `i64::MAX`) — tested alongside the refusals.

The existing comments show the wrap was deliberate: *"reinterpret the bits … without the precision loss an f64 cast would introduce."* Avoiding `f64` loss was the right instinct; bit-reinterpretation is not a way to get it, because the column really does hold a negative afterwards.

### #461 — `--window 1d` drifted off local midnight across DST `[tier-2]`

Absolute stepping meant the unit labelled `2026-03-08` covered **25 local hours** (00:00 → next day 01:00) and every later unit started at 01:00, so `${backfill.start_date}` stopped describing the window it named. Date-partitioned output was misassigned. Coverage was always gapless — which is exactly why the existing DST test passed.

- `parse_window` returns a new `WindowStep`: `d`/`w` are **calendar** steps, everything else absolute. `1d` and `24h` now deliberately differ across a transition.
- Calendar steps advance the *naive* local time (no DST) and re-resolve in the zone: a spring-forward gap nudges forward an hour at a time, a fall-back hour takes the earliest instant, matching how `--from`/`--to` dates already resolve. A non-advancing instant falls back to the nominal duration so the loop always terminates.
- The range-hash descriptor renders an absolute window as its seconds **exactly as before**, so a backfill already in flight keeps resuming. Calendar windows hash differently on purpose — their unit boundaries are not the old plan's, so resuming against an old marker would mix two different unit sets.

---

## Verification

- **`faucet-core`: 952 tests pass** (`quality,contract,masking,transforms,encryption,arrow`).
- **`cargo semver-checks check-release -p faucet-core`: 222 pass, no update required** — `u64_to_signed` is additive and `infer_arrow_schema`'s signature is unchanged.
- Touched connector suites pass; `cargo doc -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt` clean.
- **clippy `--all-targets --all-features` with fingerprints invalidated** (`touch` on every changed file first). That matters: the naive run passed, and only the forced run surfaced a real lint in one of my new tests. It is the same false-pass that cost an iteration on #457.
- The three exact slim `cargo build --no-default-features` CI commands pass.
- Not run locally: the Docker-gated integration tests (no Docker on this machine — `SocketNotFoundError`), and `--workspace --all-features`, which needs the bundled-DuckDB build this disk cannot hold. Both run in CI.

## Notes for review

- **`faucet-cli`'s lib API changes**: `backfill::plan::parse_window` now returns `WindowStep` instead of `Duration`, and `plan_windows` takes it. This is breaking for anyone depending on `faucet_cli` as a library. It is *inherent* to the fix — a `Duration` cannot express "calendar day vs 24 hours" — but `semver-checks` in CI only gates `faucet-core`, so nothing will catch it automatically. Flagging it so `faucet-cli` gets a deliberate version decision rather than a silent patch bump from the `fix:` prefix.
- `#460`'s refusal paths change behaviour for configs that "worked" before by silently corrupting. That is intended, and the error names the field and the `cast` workaround.
- Areas still unaudited after this pass: the `conformance` crate, `catalog.rs` merge logic, `livemetrics`/`progress`/`tui`, and the remaining per-connector decode paths (nats, pubsub, sqs beyond ack ordering, kinesis beyond #321). #460 came out of exactly this kind of gap-fill, so a third pass over those would likely find more.

content.text:
Audited every pending area and fixed all three findings in one PR: **[#463](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/pull/463)**, auto-merge armed.

## The audit

| Area | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Arrow columnar shim + `transform-sql` shovel | **bug — #460** |
| `backfill/plan.rs` window/DST math | **bug — #461** |
| Numeric bind paths, all SQL backends | **bug — #462**, plus 2 instances the issue didn't name |
| `adaptive.rs` | clean |
| Singer subprocess lifecycle | clean |
| `encryption.rs` (nonce/keys) | clean |
| Cluster Mode B shard fencing | clean |
| `select.rs`, `HashJoin` guard | clean |
| azure-blob / sftp bookmarks | clean |
| clickhouse / databricks / delta decode | clean |

"Clean" with reasons, since that's a claim too: singer checks the tap's exit status *before* yielding the trailing page (so a failed tap never commits an un-checkpointed page); shard reclaim re-checks the lease predicate **in the UPDATE**, not just the SELECT, so there's no TOCTOU; encryption uses a fresh random nonce per seal; `adaptive`'s validation even rejects NaN.

## The fixes

**#462 turned out to be wider than filed.** The issue named Redshift; auditing the class found the identical `u64 as i64` wrap in the **postgres and sqlite sources** too — and those bind incremental bookmarks, so `WHERE key > $1` was comparing against a negative bound: data loss/duplication, not just a bad value. `mysql` is the in-tree control that proves it — same classification, but it binds `as_u64()` directly because MySQL has a native `UNSIGNED BIGINT`. All three signed backends now refuse via a shared `u64_to_signed`.

**#460** existed twice because the arrow-json inference call was duplicated in core and `transform-sql`. Fixed once, with the shovel delegating — and the unrepresentable cases (mixed sign, wide integer inside a list) now fail loudly rather than leaving a quieter version of the same hole.

**#461** — `1d` is now a calendar day; `24h` stays elapsed time. Absolute windows keep their old range-hash so in-flight backfills still resume, while calendar windows hash differently on purpose.

## Verification

952 core tests, semver-checks 222/222 no-bump, docs `-D warnings` clean, all three exact slim CI builds clean.

Clippy earned its keep again: the naive run passed, and only the run with **fingerprints invalidated** surfaced a real lint in one of my new tests — the same false-pass that cost an iteration on #457. I now run it that way by default.

## Two things to flag

**`faucet-cli`'s lib API breaks**: `parse_window` returns `WindowStep` instead of `Duration`. That's inherent — a `Duration` can't express "calendar day vs 24 hours" — but CI's `semver-checks` only gates `faucet-core`, so nothing will catch it. It needs a deliberate version decision rather than the patch bump my `fix:` prefix implies.

**Still unaudited**: the `conformance` crate, `catalog.rs` merge logic, `livemetrics`/`progress`/`tui`, and the remaining decode paths (nats, pubsub, sqs beyond ack ordering, kinesis beyond #321). #460 came out of exactly this kind of gap-fill, so a third pass would likely find more — say the word.

---
name: reference_pre_push_gate_checklist
description: The exact local command set to run before pushing to faucet-stream; running a subset has repeatedly cost CI iterations.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Every CI iteration lost on faucet-stream PRs #457 and #463 came from running a *gate* in a state where it could not see the change. Run all of these before the first push, not a subset:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/1.96.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin:$PATH"

content.text:
`Coverage` failed, fixed, and pushed (`7eca6ceb`).

**The cause:** `cli/tests/backfill_end_to_end.rs` still constructed a `BackfillRange` with a `chrono::Duration` window, so it failed to compile under `--all-features` and took `Coverage` down. I confirmed from the log it was the **only** error, identical across all three retry attempts — so the one-line fix covers it.

**Why I missed it:** I ran `cargo test --lib backfill` and the three slim `cargo build` commands. None of those compile the CLI's *integration test* targets. A public type change in `cli/src` breaks `cli/tests/*.rs`, and `--lib` never looks there.

Now verified with the check that would have caught it — `cargo check -p faucet-cli --all-targets` over a broad feature set (clean), plus the test itself under its gating features (`source-sqlite`/`sink-sqlite`): 2 passed. I also ran `transform-sql`'s **integration** tests, which I'd previously only run at `--lib`: 15 + 1 + 23, all green.

## On the pattern

That's five CI iterations across these two PRs, and every one was the same failure mode: **I ran a gate in a state where it couldn't see my change.** Clippy reusing stale fingerprints. `--lib` not compiling sibling tests. `semver-checks` never run at all the first time. Each individually defensible, collectively a process gap.

I've written it down as a memory — the exact command sequence, in order, with `touch` on changed files *first* so clippy actually re-analyses, and the feature-set artifacts to expect locally so I don't chase them as regressions. Two narrower notes already existed and I violated both, so this one consolidates them into a single thing to run.

The one you may want to act on: **`faucet-cli`'s lib API breaks** (`parse_window` → `WindowStep`). It's inherent to the DST fix, but CI's `semver-checks` only gates `faucet-core`, so nothing will flag it — and my `fix:` commit prefix implies a patch bump. Worth a deliberate version call before release-plz picks it up.

Watching CI; will report when it merges.

---
name: reference_pre_push_gate_checklist
description: The exact local command set to run before pushing to faucet-stream; running a subset has repeatedly cost CI iterations.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: c52ee385-5ec5-464a-91ae-a39a0cbdf230

Every CI iteration lost on faucet-stream PRs #457 and #463 came from running a *gate* in a state where it could not see the change. Run all of these before the first push, not a subset:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/1.96.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin:$PATH"
export RUSTC=$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/1.96.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc

# 1. Invalidate fingerprints FIRST — clippy silently reuses cached analysis
#    after a `cargo test` on the same files and reports a false pass.
for f in $(git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD -- '*.rs'); do touch "$f"; done

# 2. clippy, --all-targets (lib-only misses sibling test files)
cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# 3. Compile EVERY target of the changed crate, not just --lib / one --test.
#    A public type change breaks cli/tests/*.rs, which --lib never compiles.
cargo check -p faucet-cli --all-targets --features "<broad set, no duckdb>"

# 4. Public-API break check (CI gates faucet-core ONLY — faucet-cli is unguarded)
cargo semver-checks check-release -p faucet-core

# 5. Docs: an orphaned intra-doc link fails the required Docs job
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p <crate> --all-features --no-deps

# 6. The three exact slim CLI builds from ci.yml (catches feature-gating misses)
for f in "source-rest,sink-jsonl,sink-stdout,transforms" \
         "observability,source-rest,sink-jsonl,sink-stdout,transforms" \
         "otel,source-rest,sink-jsonl,sink-stdout,transforms"; do
  cargo build -p faucet-cli --no-default-features --features "$f"; done

cargo fmt --all --check
```

**Feature-set artifacts to expect locally** (not regressions): `commands/fmt` key-order tests fail without a `preserve_order`-enabling dep (`bson`/`object_store` — add `sink-mongodb`); `replication::compiled` + `commands::conformance` need `source-postgres`; `commands/template.rs`'s `BODY` const reads as dead code without `serve-history-sqlite`; `preview.rs` imports look unused without source/sink features.

Related: [[reference_clippy_cache_false_pass]], [[reference_verify_all_targets_before_push]], [[reference_all_features_cannot_link_locally]].

**This one is squarely on me, and worse than the last:** for `faucet-cli` I substituted `cargo check --all-targets` for `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` to save a build. `unused_imports` is a *warning*, so `check` passed while the Clippy job failed. I ran real clippy on core and the connector crates, but took the shortcut on the one crate where all my CLI changes live.

The sharper detail: **the checklist I wrote one message ago contained this exact flaw** — its step 3 said `cargo check --all-targets`. I encoded the shortcut into the very note meant to prevent the mistake, then followed it. I've corrected the memory to merge those steps into a single `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` across *every* changed crate, with both traps spelled out so the substitution isn't available next time.

Re-ran the real gate afterward — clean.

**PR state:** 114 pass, `Clippy` was the only failure. `API stability`, `Docs`, and `CLI build (full)` are green; `Coverage` and `Test` were still running and are the ones that matter now (`Coverage` is where the `backfill_end_to_end` fix gets confirmed). Auto-merge armed.

Six iterations on this branch, all mine. I'm not going to pretend that's a good ratio — the fixes themselves have held up under CI each time, but my pre-push discipline has been the bottleneck, and the correction that matters is the one now in the checklist rather than anything in the diff.

content.text:
**Merged** — `00065815` on `main`, all checks green, branch auto-deleted, and **#460, #461, #462 all closed** automatically. Local `main` synced.

## Where the whole effort landed

Two audits, two merged PRs, **22 verified defects fixed**:

| | PR #457 | PR #463 |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | 5 | 2 (`#460`, `#462`) |
| High | 5 | — |
| Medium | 5 | 1 (`#461`) |
| Low | 4 | — |

The second pass mattered more than its count suggests: **#462 was wider than the issue I filed** — auditing the class found the same `u64 as i64` wrap in the postgres and sqlite sources, which also bind incremental bookmarks, making it a data-loss path rather than just a bad value. And **#460 existed twice** because one inference call was duplicated; it's now one implementation.

## Still open, deliberately

- **[#458](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/458)** — topology exactly-once (currently rejected outright, not silently downgraded).
- **[#459](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/issues/459)** — topology notifications/lineage/catalog/SLA (now warned about, not wired). The notify gap is the operationally sharp one.

Both tier-2, on epic #38.

## Two things for you

**`faucet-cli`'s lib API broke** (`parse_window` → `WindowStep`). Inherent to the DST fix, but CI's `semver-checks` only gates `faucet-core`, so release-plz will read my `fix:` prefix as a patch bump. That needs a deliberate call before the next release.

**A third pass would likely find more.** Still unaudited: the `conformance` crate, `catalog.rs` merge logic, `livemetrics`/`progress`/`tui`, and the decode paths for nats/pubsub/sqs beyond ack ordering. I say "likely" because that's precisely how #460 surfaced — the areas I'd deprioritised turned out to hold a tier-1.

## On my own execution

Seven CI iterations across the two PRs, six of them my own misses. The fixes held up every time; the pre-push discipline didn't. The most useful artifact may be the corrected checklist in memory — including the part where the *first* version of that checklist contained the very shortcut (`cargo check` instead of `clippy -D warnings`) that caused the last failure. Worth converting into a real pre-push script in the repo rather than leaving it as my private note.

content.text: Both `RunLifecycle` and `CatalogUpdate` hard-code **one input dataset** — but a topology sink can be fed by N sources (merge/join). That's a data-model limitation, not a wiring gap, and resolving it means changing two *published* crates' public APIs. That's your call, so let me ask while I implement the parts that aren't blocked.

questions.question: Lineage and catalog both model exactly one input dataset per run (`RunLifecycle.input`, `CatalogUpdate.source`). A topology sink fed by a merge/join has several. How should I handle it?

options.label: Extend both to N inputs (Recommended)
options.description: Change RunLifecycle.input → inputs: Vec and CatalogUpdate.source → sources: Vec, so merge/join graphs are recorded correctly. Closes #459 fully. Cost: breaking public API change to faucet-lineage and the catalog store (~250 lines incl. memory+SQL backends); semver-checks only gates faucet-core so CI won't flag it — both crates need a deliberate version bump. OpenLineage's own RunEvent already models inputs as a list, so this aligns us with the spec.

options.label: Single-source sinks only, follow-up for N:1
options.description: Wire lineage+catalog where the 1:1 model is exact (linear and tee graphs — the large majority), and keep the explicit warning for a multi-source sink rather than writing volume numbers that would corrupt catalog stats and SLA baselines. #459 stays open as 'Addresses', with a focused follow-up issue for the model extension. No API break.

options.label: Notify + SLA only this PR
options.description: Ship the two that need no model change (notify is the operationally sharp one — a topology run can currently fail with no alert). Leave lineage+catalog entirely to a follow-up. Smallest, safest diff; #459 stays substantially open.

Closes #458. Addresses #459 (notify + SLA; catalog + lineage follow in the
next commit).

#458 — replaces the blanket \`delivery: exactly_once\` rejection with the real
per-node requirements, checked at config-load time so an unsupportable config
is still never silently downgraded (the #456 H2 invariant):

  1. exactly one source node — a sink's watermark is only meaningful against a
     known source position, and nothing records which source fed a page;
  2. that source replays deterministically;
  3. *every* sink node commits data + token atomically (each keeps its own
     watermark, so one non-qualifying sink disqualifies the run);
  4. durable non-memory \`state:\`;
  5. no \`dlq:\`.

Messages name the limiting side and offer the keyed-upsert alternative, the
same shape as the matrix gate in \`expand\`, so moving a pipeline between the two
forms reads the same diagnosis. \`resolved_node_kind\` mirrors
\`resolve_connector\`'s kind precedence so the gate and the builder cannot
disagree about what a node is.

#459 — \`run_reported\` gives per-node attribution, so each **sink node** now
gets its own SLA evaluation (under its own \`{pipeline}::{node}\` state key) and
its own notification, success or failure. A topology run that fails no longer
does so silently. Both are thin adapters over the standalone functions the
matrix executor already calls, not a parallel implementation. Failures are also
attributed to their node in the run summary instead of a flat \"topology\" row.

Also fixes a bug I introduced in #457: \`inert_blocks\` listed \`resilience\` as
ignored while \`build_governance\` was wiring it — a false warning. Removed, with
a test asserting validate does not claim it is ignored." && git log --oneline -2

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Rust workspace, 91 crates; `faucet-core` (traits/pipeline/topology), `faucet-cli`, `faucet-lineage`, connector crates.
   - Topology mode (`pipeline.nodes`/`edges`): typed node graph (source/transform/tee/merge/join/sink), bounded mpsc channels, one tokio task per node.

       ```rust
